title: Chemistry 12 — Mission 1: The Slow Reaction
description: A production reaction is taking three times longer than the manual says. Diagnose what's throttling the rate before the client shipment slips.

mika.name: Ms. Mika Tan
mika.description: Treats every slow reaction as a rate-law puzzle, not a mystery.

dev.name: Dev
dev.description: Wants to just add more of everything and hope it speeds up.

rate_law_notes.name: Rate Law Notes
rate_law_notes.description: Collision theory, activation energy, and the factors that change reaction rate.

catalyst_sample.name: Catalyst Sample
catalyst_sample.description: A small vial that might be the missing variable.

elements.text: This reaction usually finishes in twenty minutes. Today it's been over an hour and it's still going.
Let's just dump in more reactant, that should speed it up, right?

elements.prompt: Mika hands you the rate law notes.

options.text: "Not yet — let's check what actually changed: temperature, concentration, surface area, or a missing catalyst."

elements.text: Good, notes in hand. Let's work through what's actually throttling this.
No notes yet — we're just guessing without them. Let's fix that.

config.question: According to collision theory, for a reaction to occur when particles collide, they must:

options.text: Collide with enough energy (at least the activation energy) and correct orientation
Simply touch, regardless of energy or orientation
Be the same temperature as each other

config.explanation: A collision only leads to reaction if particles have at least the activation energy and hit with a favorable orientation.

config.prompt: Dev checks the log: the batch was mixed at 15 degrees C today instead of the usual 25 degrees C. Lower temperature means fewer particles have enough energy to react. What factor is throttling the rate? (one word)
Order these fixes from least to most disruptive way to speed the reaction back up.

items.text: Reheat the mixture to the usual 25 degrees C
Add a catalyst to lower the activation energy
Scrap the batch and start over from raw materials

elements.text: Reheated to spec and the reaction's back on schedule. The shipment makes it out today.
We got it moving again, but next time let's check the factors before adding more reactant.

elements.prompt: The batch is back on schedule. What now?

options.text: Show Dev the four factors that control reaction rate so this never causes a scare again.
Log it and move on. Good enough for today.

elements.text: So it's never just 'add more stuff' — temperature, concentration, surface area, and catalysts each do something different. I get it now.

ending.title: Rate Diagnostician
ending.description: Diagnosed the slow reaction from collision theory alone and taught Dev the four rate factors.

ending.title: Batch Recovered
ending.description: The reaction rate is fixed and logged. The deeper rate-law lesson can wait.
